title: Restriction of modules to an open subscheme is exact and preserves injectives; direct image along the open immersion preserves injectives
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $U\subseteq X$ an open subscheme with inclusion $j:U\to X$, and for an $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal G$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] let $\mathcal G|_U$ be the restricted $\mathcal O_U$-module, $(\mathcal G|_U)(W)=\mathcal G(W)$ for $W\subseteq U$ open [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits]; let $j_*:\Mod(\mathcal O_U)\to\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ be the direct image, $(j_*\mathcal H)(W)=\mathcal H(W\cap U)$. Then: (1) the functor $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)\to\Mod(\mathcal O_U)$, $\mathcal G\mapsto\mathcal G|_U$, is exact [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]: it is additive and carries a sequence of $\mathcal O_X$-modules exact at the middle term to one exact at the middle term; (2) if $\mathcal I$ is an injective $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sp-injective-resolutions], then $\mathcal I|_U$ is an injective $\mathcal O_U$-module; (3) if $\mathcal J$ is an injective $\mathcal O_U$-module, then $j_*\mathcal J$ is an injective $\mathcal O_X$-module. Consequently, if $\mathcal F\to\mathcal I^\bullet$ is an injective resolution of an $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$ in $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$, then $\mathcal F|_U\to\mathcal I^\bullet|_U$ is an injective resolution of $\mathcal F|_U$ in $\Mod(\mathcal O_U)$.

source.place: Cohomology of Sheaves, Lemma 01E1 (lemma-cohomology-of-open, line 495) part (1) and its proof (restriction is right adjoint to the exact extension by zero j_!, Sheaves Lemma 00A7 (sheaves-lemma-j-shriek-modules), so Homology Lemma 015Z (homology-lemma-adjoint-preserve-injectives) applies; 'F|_U -> I^bullet|_U is an injective resolution'); for (3) Cohomology Lemma 02N5 (lemma-pushforward-injective-flat, line 1820: f_* of an injective is injective for flat f, an open immersion being flat), equivalently 015Z for the adjunction (-)|_U -| j_* with (-)|_U exact

proof.text: (Proof of (1): restriction is exact, checked on stalks.) Restriction is a functor $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)\to\Mod(\mathcal O_U)$ [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits] with $(\psi|_U)_W=\psi_W$; hence it is additive ($(\psi+\psi')|_U=\psi|_U+\psi'|_U$, $0|_U=0$, sums of sections being computed sectionwise [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]) and carries complexes to complexes. Stalks: let $x\in U$ and $\mathcal G$ an $\mathcal O_X$-module. Define $c_x:(\mathcal G|_U)_x\to\mathcal G_x$ by sending the germ at $x$ of $s\in(\mathcal G|_U)(W)=\mathcal G(W)$ ($x\in W\subseteq U$) to the germ $s_x\in\mathcal G_x$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. It is well defined and injective: by the description of equality of germs in [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], $s,s'$ (over $W,W'\subseteq U$) have the same germ in $\mathcal G_x$ iff they agree on some open $x\in W''\subseteq W\cap W'$, and such $W''$ lies in $U$, which is also the condition for equality in $(\mathcal G|_U)_x$. It is surjective: every element of $\mathcal G_x$ is a germ $t_x$ with $t\in\mathcal G(V)$, $x\in V$, and $t_x$ is the image of the germ of $t|_{V\cap U}$. It is $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-linear (the ring stalks $\mathcal O_{U,x}\to\mathcal O_{X,x}$ are identified by the same argument) and natural: $c_x\circ(\psi|_U)_x=\psi_x\circ c_x$, both sending the germ of $s$ to $\psi_W(s)_x$. Now let $\mathcal F\xrightarrow{\varphi}\mathcal G\xrightarrow{\psi}\mathcal H$ be a complex of $\mathcal O_X$-modules exact at $\mathcal G$ [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact] (5) on $X$, $\mathcal F_x\to\mathcal G_x\to\mathcal H_x$ is exact at $\mathcal G_x$ for every $x\in X$. For $x\in U$ the isomorphisms $c_x$ identify $(\mathcal F|_U)_x\to(\mathcal G|_U)_x\to(\mathcal H|_U)_x$ with this sequence (naturality), so it is exact at $(\mathcal G|_U)_x$. $U$ is a scheme, so [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact] (5) on $U$ shows that $\mathcal F|_U\to\mathcal G|_U\to\mathcal H|_U$ is exact at $\mathcal G|_U$. Hence restriction is exact; in particular it carries short exact sequences to short exact sequences and monomorphisms to monomorphisms.

proof.text: (Proof of (2): restriction preserves injectives.) Let $j_!:\Mod(\mathcal O_U)\to\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ be extension by zero [lem-weil-pbc-module-extension-by-zero-adjunction]; it is an additive functor (ibid. (1)) and left adjoint to $\mathcal G\mapsto\mathcal G|_U$ (ibid. (2)). It is exact: let $\mathcal F'\xrightarrow{\alpha}\mathcal F\xrightarrow{\beta}\mathcal F''$ be a complex of $\mathcal O_U$-modules exact at $\mathcal F$; then $j_!\mathcal F'\to j_!\mathcal F\to j_!\mathcal F''$ is a complex ($j_!\beta\circ j_!\alpha=j_!(\beta\alpha)=0$). For $x\in X\setminus U$ its stalks are $0\to0\to0$ (ibid. (3)), exact. For $x\in U$ the natural isomorphisms of ibid. (3) identify its stalk sequence with $\mathcal F'_x\to\mathcal F_x\to\mathcal F''_x$, which is exact at $\mathcal F_x$ by [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact] (5) on the scheme $U$. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact] (5) on $X$, $j_!\mathcal F'\to j_!\mathcal F\to j_!\mathcal F''$ is exact at $j_!\mathcal F$. So $j_!$ is an exact functor between the abelian categories $\Mod(\mathcal O_U)$, $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] with right adjoint the restriction, and [lem-sp-right-adjoint-preserves-injectives] (with $u=j_!$, $u_*=(-)|_U$) gives: if $\mathcal I$ is an injective $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sp-injective-resolutions], then $\mathcal I|_U$ is an injective $\mathcal O_U$-module.

source.place: Cohomology, Lemma 01E1 (label lemma-cohomology-of-open, line 495), proof of (1): restriction is right adjoint to j_! proof.text: (Proof of (3): $j_*$ preserves injectives.) By [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits] (1), applied to the open immersion $j:U\to X$, restriction $\mathcal G\mapsto\mathcal G|_U$ is left adjoint to the direct image $j_*$, $(j_*\mathcal H)(W)=\mathcal H(j^{-1}W)=\mathcal H(W\cap U)$. By Step 1 restriction is an exact functor between the abelian categories $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ and $\Mod(\mathcal O_U)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. So [lem-sp-right-adjoint-preserves-injectives] (with $u=(-)|_U$, $u_*=j_*$) gives: if $\mathcal J$ is an injective $\mathcal O_U$-module [def-sp-injective-resolutions], then $j_*\mathcal J$ is an injective $\mathcal O_X$-module.

source.place: Cohomology, Lemma 02N5 (label lemma-pushforward-injective-flat, line 1824) and its proof (f^* transforms injections into injections, so Homology Lemma 015Z applies to f^* ⊣ f_*), for f = j, where f^* = restriction is exact by Step 1

proof.text: (Consequence: restrictions of injective resolutions.) Let $\mathcal F\to\mathcal I^\bullet$ be an injective resolution in $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions]: each $\mathcal I^p$ is injective, $\mathcal I^p=0$ for $p$ small, and the augmented complex $0\to\mathcal F\to\mathcal I^0\to\mathcal I^1\to\cdots$ (indexing so that the cohomology of $\mathcal I^\bullet$ is $\mathcal F$ in degree $0$ and zero elsewhere) is exact at every term [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]. Restriction carries this complex to the complex $0\to\mathcal F|_U\to\mathcal I^0|_U\to\mathcal I^1|_U\to\cdots$ ($0|_U=0$), which is exact at every term by Step 1; each $\mathcal I^p|_U$ is injective by Step 2, and $\mathcal I^p|_U=0$ whenever $\mathcal I^p=0$. $\Mod(\mathcal O_U)$ is abelian with enough injectives, $U$ being a scheme [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-modules-enough-injectives]. Hence $\mathcal F|_U\to\mathcal I^\bullet|_U$ is an injective resolution of $\mathcal F|_U$ in $\Mod(\mathcal O_U)$.
